title: Build Harbor Relay Trivia & Scoreboard
summary: Build the game from one shared prompt. Score your first file with the same five checks as the other tools.
requires: You need access to the tool for the build, an empty practice folder, and a browser to play the saved file. For the fit check, use an iPad or an iPad-sized browser view and record which you used.
features: ChatGPT Work can return a file. Codex can build one in a practice folder.
roles: Use the same pretend mail report to check whether a double tap counts a row twice.
Give four helpers the same made-up team list. Check that each turn goes to the right team.
Build one small game four ways. Choose the one you enjoy playing and editing.
prompt: Build a single-file offline web app (`index.html`) for a two-team pass-and-play game called Harbor Relay. Use a clean, bright, high-contrast theme that works on both iPad and desktop screens. Include: (1) Team Blue and Team Gold starting at 0 points, (2) a deck of 6 built-in harbor trivia questions with 3 multiple-choice buttons each, (3) +2 points for a correct answer and 0 points for a wrong answer, automatically switching turns after each answer, (4) a visible Question X of 6 counter and a short explanation after each pick, (5) locking the answer buttons after a pick and after question 6 ends the game, and (6) a Play Again button that resets both scores to 0, resets to Team Blue, and returns to Question 1.

steps.title: Open Work or Codex
steps.text: Open ChatGPT, choose Work and start a new task. For Codex, open an empty practice folder and start a new task there. Choose one route for this run.
steps.help: Check the folder or task name at the top. The new task should have no old files, messages or project instructions.

steps.title: Send the shared prompt once
steps.text: Copy Your prompt from this page and send it by itself. Save the first reply before asking for any changes.
steps.help: Leave the five checks in the book. All four builders get just the words in the prompt.

steps.title: Keep the first file
steps.text: In Work, open the returned file. In Codex, look in the practice folder for index.html. If you get an HTML code block, copy its contents into a plain-text file named index.html.
steps.help: Leave out the code fence marks. Keep the file just as it came back. If there is no usable HTML, record what you received.

steps.title: Play the original with the network off
steps.text: Save index.html by itself in an empty folder. Turn off Wi-Fi or unplug the network. Open the saved file in a browser that runs local HTML. Check the starting team, both scores and each of the six question numbers. Read the short explanation after every pick.
steps.help: A chat preview may work online even when the file needs the internet. Test the saved file in a fresh browser window. For iPad fit, use the same browser and screen size for all four games.

steps.title: Test both teams and the lock
steps.text: In one game, have Blue get all three turns right and Gold miss all three. On the first right answer, tap the same choice twice quickly. Look for Blue 2, Gold 0 and just one turn passed. Finish all six questions.
steps.help: Use the answers stored in the file or learn them in a practice round. Another game may ask different questions. Use the same pattern of right and wrong picks.

steps.title: Test a win, a tie and a clean replay
steps.text: The first game should end Blue 6, Gold 0. Try another answer after the end. Press Play Again and check the first turn, scores and question number. Play again with six right answers. The tie should be 6 to 6.
steps.help: On each question count the three choices. After each pick, try tapping before moving on. A score or question that changes twice is a failed lock.

steps.title: Record the first try before making an edit
steps.text: Use the five checks on this page. Give one point for each pass. Open the four-tool scorecard to record what you saw. Once you have scored the originals, use the same follow-up there for each tool.
steps.help: Keep a copy of the first file. If you have only tested one tool, leave the other scorecards blank.

check: Layout & Mobile Fit: All buttons and text fit cleanly on an iPad screen without overlapping or sideways scrolling.
Scoring & Turn Switch: Correct answers add +2 to the active team only; wrong answers add 0; turns alternate Blue -> Gold after every question.
Click-Lock Guard: Tapping an answer twice on the same question cannot award +4 points or skip a turn.
Game End & Winner: After Question 6, answer buttons lock and a clear winner (or tie) banner appears.
Clean Replay: Play Again resets both scores to 0, sets Question 1 of 6, and returns the first turn to Team Blue.

steps.text: Open a new practice folder in Codex. Paste these sample inputs into the task along with the lab request. Ask it to build the first test around these values.
steps.help: If an old project is open, choose the new empty folder before sending the request.
steps.code: Fixed board rows CAT, ORE, DOG. Targets CAT, DOG, COD. Straight paths forward or backward.

steps.title: Make the first version
steps.text: Paste the lab request into the task and send it. Read the proposed change. Open the named output file or inspect the answer.
steps.help: If you receive only a plan, ask Codex to carry it out in this practice folder and show how to run the result.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Start the local server using the command the tool gives you. Open its localhost link in a browser. Play the sample round. Tap the ends of CAT and then the ends of CAT in reverse. Only one target is checked. COD is in column one.
steps.help: Trace CAT across the first row, DOG across the last row and COD down the first column. Keep one target for the offline part of the test.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Find DOG, go offline after the app says ready, reload, then select COD from top to bottom. Restart.
steps.help: If the page fails offline, check that you first served it at localhost or HTTPS and loaded every file online.

check: Tap the ends of CAT and then the ends of CAT in reverse. Only one target is checked. COD is in column one.
The win message shows all 3. Restart clears the checks and leaves the same playable board while offline.

title: Capstone: build a mailbox report wall
summary: Make a small offline dashboard that can explain every total to a reader.
requires: Open Codex on a Mac or PC. Give it a fresh practice folder. Use “First time here?” to find the steps for opening it.
features: A report can have a real zero and still have missing data on another row. Separate those cases before adding anything.
roles: Check mail totals without touching Exchange.
Hand a tested dashboard to a team.
Ship an app that can explain its numbers.
prompt: Build a local HTML report app with CSV input, a preview, type filters and a downloadable summary. Show included boxes, known item sum, missing-count rows and excluded rooms. Flag repeated IDs and never replace a good report with a bad import. Include a test file and buttons or commands to run the checks.

steps.title: Give the app its own folder
steps.text: Open a new practice folder in Codex. Paste these sample inputs into the task along with the lab request. Ask it to build the first test around these values.
steps.help: If an old project is open, choose the new empty folder before sending the request.
steps.code: Box A shared 4; B user 0; C room 3; D shared blank. Group by type. Only user and shared boxes belong.

steps.title: Make the first version
steps.text: Paste the lab request into the task and send it. Read the proposed change. Open the named output file or inspect the answer.
steps.help: If you receive only a plan, ask Codex to carry it out in this practice folder and show how to run the result.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Open index.html in a browser, or use the local preview link if the app needs a server. Try the sample. The included count is 3. Known items sum to 4. One count is missing and one room is excluded. The user filter shows B with 0.
steps.help: Make separate notes for included boxes, known item sum and missing counts. B increases the first total by one and the second by zero.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Save the good summary. Add a second A with count 9 and try to import. Then fix D to 2 in a clean copy and import it.
steps.help: If the duplicate silently wins, ask for a whole-file ID check before the preview can become the current report.

check: The included count is 3. Known items sum to 4. One count is missing and one room is excluded. The user filter shows B with 0.
The duplicate is rejected and the good summary stays. Fixing D gives 6 known items and no missing count.
